Title: Syed Azman raises HHRG stake after taking chairman's seat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Newly-appointed executive chairman Tan Sri Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim has raised his stake in biomass company HHRG Bhd by more than 4.7 million shares.
Syed Azman bought 4.72 million shares or a 0.36 per cent stake at 18.15 sen for RM857,333 on Wednesday,
according to a bourse filing on Thursday.
This came less than a week after he took the helm of the company.
The purchase price was 3.7 per cent above HHRG's closing price of 17.5 sen on Wednesday.
Following the acquisition, Syed Azman's stake in HHRG stood at 3.21 per cent, keeping him below the five per cent threshold for substantial shareholders.
Syed Azman, founder of helicopter services firm Weststar Aviation, joined HHRG's board on Sept 4 and became executive chairman, filling a position vacant for more than two years.
The latest share purchase comes as HHRG reshuffles its leadership.
On Thursday, the company redesignated executive deputy chairman Datuk Ammar Shaikh Mahmood Naim as executive director, without naming a successor for the deputy chairman position.
Ammar, 64, was Kedah state secretary from December 2018 until his retirement in 2022.
He joined HHRG's board in June 2024 and subsequently oversaw the company's operations after former group executive chairman H'ng Choon Seng stepped down that month for unspecified personal reasons.
HHRG's annual report said Ammar oversees the group's business development.
He currently holds 310,000 shares, or a 0.025 per cent stake, in the company.
HHRG's largest shareholders are Ch'ng Chen Mong and Tan Poh Cheng, who collectively hold 14.53 per cent, followed by H'ng and Goh Boon Leong with a combined 11.32 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit firmer against US dollar ahead of US CPI data
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed marginally higher against the US dollar on Thursday despite elevated crude oil prices and expectations of a possible US interest rate hike, as investors looked ahead to the release of US consumer price index (CPI) data on Friday.
At 6pm, the local currency appreciated to 4.0630/0670 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0670/0720.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude was hovering around US$101 per barrel, a development that could bolster the case for a rate hike at next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"Despite that, the ringgit performed favourably against the US dollar. Still, it remains to be seen whether the appreciation can be sustained in the near term," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said the US inflation reading, due on Friday, would be closely watched for indications on the Federal Reserve's policy path, which could influence the ringgit's near-term direction.
At the close, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened slightly against the euro to 4.7269/7315 from Wednesday's 4.7275/7333 and appreciated against the Japanese yen to 2.6431/6459 from 2.6474/6509.
Against the British pound, it was little changed at 5.5046/5100 from 5.5043/5110 previously.
The ringgit also traded higher against Asean currencies.
It strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2113/2148 from 3.2150/2192, appreciated against the Thai baht to 12.3331/3497 from 12.3579/3788, rose against the Indonesian rupiah to 231.5/231.8 from 232.2/232.6, and improved against the Philippine peso to 6.49/6.50 from 6.50/6.52 at yesterday's close.

Title: Missing person case reclassified as murder after man found dead in septic tank
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Police have reclassified a missing person case as murder after a man was found dead in a septic tank at a house in Taman Seri Bistari here yesterday.
Seberang Prai Selatan deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Norazmi Abd Ghapar said a missing-person report was lodged on Sept 7, prompting an immediate investigation.
A
body
was subsequently discovered at the premises yesterday after residents reported a foul stench coming from the house.
"A post-mortem was conducted today, with the identity of the deceased confirmed.
"Based on the post-mortem findings and developments in the investigation, police have reclassified the case from Section 365 of the Penal Code for abduction to Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder," Norazmi said tonight.
He said police are investigating the motive and circumstances of the incident and working to identify and arrest those involved.
Those with information can contact investigating officer Assistant Superintendent Jegathiswaran Chanthirasegaran at 04-585 8222 or the nearest police station.
The victim's family had earlier lodged a missing person's report in the Seberang Prai Tengah district.
Earlier today, five people were remanded for four days to assist investigations into the abduction of a man whose body was found in the septic tank.
The suspects comprised three Malaysians, including the house owner, and two Myanmar nationals, a man and a woman.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Akmal tells PH to forget BN cooperation for Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has challenged Pakatan Harapan to contest all 28 seats in the next Melaka state election, telling the coalition to forget about working with Barisan Nasional.
"After this, we will face the Melaka state election. Forget about working with BN. Contest all 28 seats.
"I really cannot wait to take on Pakatan Harapan in all 28 seats in Melaka," he said in his winding-up speech at the Umno Youth delegates' conference here today.
Dr Akmal then asked delegates whether they were ready to take on PH and whether they could win, drawing cries of "Boleh!" from the floor.
He also urged the party leadership to involve Umno Youth in drafting BN's manifesto for the next general election, saying the wing's priority was to help shape policies rather than secure candidacies.
"On candidates, if we get selected, we get selected. Even if we do not, we will still work to ensure our party wins. But in preparing for the next election, we want to be involved in drawing up the manifesto," he said.
Dr Akmal said issues raised by delegates should be incorporated into BN's manifesto, adding that the party could not seek young voters' support while excluding its youth wing from the process.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IHH Healthcare unit loses RM5.7bil claim against Japan's pharmaceutical giant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd's Singapore-based unit Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd has lost a ¥200 billion (about RM5.7 billion) damages claim against Japanese pharmaceutical giant Daiichi Sankyo Co Ltd, after a Tokyo court dismisses all its claims.
The Tokyo District Court on Thursday dismissed Northern TK's legal claims and ordered the IHH unit to bear the litigation costs, IHH said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
The claim, initially filed for ¥20 billion, was expanded to about ¥200 billion in May 2025 following an assessment of the losses Northern TK alleged it suffered due to its stalled Fortis Healthcare acquisition.
IHH said Northern TK disagreed with the court's decision and remains confident in the merits of its position.
It is reviewing the judgment in detail with its legal counsel and evaluating all legal remedies available to pursue the relief it believes is warranted.
"Northern TK remains committed to vigorously protecting its rights and interests through every appropriate legal channel," it said.
The claim stemmed from IHH's 2018 acquisition of a 31 per cent stake in Indian hospital operator Fortis Healthcare Ltd through Northern TK, after which it planned to acquire a further 26 per cent stake through an open offer.
However, the planned acquisition was halted after Daiichi Sankyo filed a contempt plea against Fortis' former promoters, Malvinder Singh and Shivinder Singh, in connection with a separate dispute arising from Daiichi's acquisition of Ranbaxy Laboratories.
Daiichi had won an arbitration award against the brothers due to its 2008 acquisition of Ranbaxy and was seeking to enforce the award in India.
Northern TK later alleged that Daiichi's actions prevented it from proceeding with the open offer and caused financial losses.
It filed a claim against Daiichi at the Tokyo District Court in October 2023, initially seeking ¥20 billion in damages.
In May 2025, Northern TK sought to substantially increase the damages claim to as much as 200 billion yen.
The revised claim was based on an expert report that estimated potential damages at between ¥7.8 billion and ¥199.8 billion.
IHH currently holds a 31.17 per cent stake in Fortis and plans to gradually increase its interest to 51 per cent in about four years.

Title: Malaysia property market remains resilient with RM105.12bil transactions in 1H 2026 – Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's property market remained resilient, recording 187,320 transactions worth RM105.12 billion in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said.
He said the performance was in line with Malaysia's robust economic growth, with gross domestic product (GDP) expanding 6.0 per cent in the second quarter.
"Despite some marginal adjustments, the property market remained firm, supported by stable transaction activity and price movements, as well as active construction activity.
"This stability was underpinned by the country's monetary policy, with the overnight policy rate (OPR) maintained at 2.75 per cent, providing confidence to financiers and buyers," he said in his speech at the launch of the 1H 2026 Property Market Report today.
Amir Hamzah said 27,832 new residential units were launched in 1H 2026, with a sales performance of 16.6 per cent.
The Malaysia House Price Index stood at 234.7 points, with the average house price at RM506,317 per unit, representing marginal annual growth of 0.9 per cent, he said.
At the same time, Amir Hamzah said the commercial property market also supported the resilience of the broader economy, with the overall occupancy rate for purpose-built offices for both the private and government sectors rising to 78.5 per cent in 1H 2026 from 77.8 per cent in 1H 2025.
For shopping complexes, the overall occupancy rate remained stable at 77.9 per cent nationwide, compared with 78.7 per cent in 1H 2025, he said.
"The industrial property segment also grew 3.8 per cent, recording 3,932 transactions worth RM14.78 billion.
"This development was in line with robust growth in the country's manufacturing sector, which expanded 7.3 per cent in the second quarter of 2026," he said.
During 1H 2026, the residential subsector accounted for 59.3 per cent of total property transactions, with 110,998 transactions.
In value terms, the residential subsector also accounted for the largest share, at 44.8 per cent of total property transaction value, amounting to RM47.11 billion.
Despite the market's resilience, Amir Hamzah said 33,094 completed but unsold residential units were recorded, with a total value of RM17.78 billion, compared with 30,471 units worth RM17.73 billion in 1Q 2025.
Asked about the outlook for the property sector in the second half of 2026, Amir Hamzah said positive labour market momentum, including a low unemployment rate and rising wages, was expected to continue supporting demand for property.
He said government measures to address the cost of living, including the implementation of minimum wage policies and targeted assistance initiatives, would also help raise Malaysians' disposable income and strengthen homebuyer confidence.

Title: LSH Capital gets nod to build, operate RM1.75bil Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan expressway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lim Seong Hai Capital Bhd (LSH Capital) has received in-principle approval from the Cabinet to undertake the proposed RM1.75 billion Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Expressway (BSE).
It will be undertaken under a build-operate-transfer privatisation arrangement, LSH Capital said in a statement.
The company said the Works Ministry informed it that the Cabinet had agreed in principle to implement the 8.2-kilometre expressway.
It will connect the Salak Interchange on the Setiawangsa-Pantai Expressway (SPE) near Bandar Malaysia to the Sungai Besi Toll Plaza on the North-South Expressway (PLUS).
The project will also include a spur link to the Maju Expressway (MEX) via the Bukit Jalil Highway.
The BSE is expected to comprise four interchanges and three ramps, providing connectivity to several major highways and roads.
This includes the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, SPE, East-West Link Expressway, New Pantai Expressway, Sungai Besi Expressway, MEX and PLUS.
It is envisaged as a highway-to-highway connector to improve connectivity between existing road networks and facilitate access to the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway, East Coast Expressway, New Klang Valley Expressway and PLUS.
LSH Capital said the project, which has an estimated construction cost of RM1.75 billion excluding sales and services tax, is expected to take four years to complete.
The BSE will be undertaken through a special purpose vehicle equally owned by Pertama Makmur Sdn Bhd and LSH Infra Sdn Bhd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of LSH Capital.
The proposed concession period is 60 years, including the construction period.
LSH Capital said the project would strengthen its construction and facilities management portfolio while contributing to its recurring income base.
Upon completion, the company's facilities management division is expected to have opportunities to participate in the expressway's operations and maintenance as well as related support services throughout the concession period.
The company said based on preliminary estimates, operations and maintenance activities for the BSE could contribute about RM20 million in revenue in the first year of operations.
The project is also expected to support more than 100 trades across the construction supply chain and create about 15,000 jobs during the construction phase.
LSH Capital chairman Tan Sri Lim Keng Cheng said the project marked a transformational milestone for the group and would strengthen its position in the construction and facilities management sectors.
"This concession will enable us to build a long-term infrastructure portfolio supported by stable and recurring income streams," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, India set to deepen trade, investment ties through BRICS
Article:
NEW DELHI: India's position as Malaysia's largest trading partner in Asia is giving added weight to Malaysia's efforts to leverage its BRICS participation to deepen trade, investment and economic ties with major emerging markets.
Sharifah Ezneeda Wafa, Chargé d'Affaires and Deputy High Commissioner at the High Commission of Malaysia, said bilateral investment reached US$5.6 billion in 2025, involving Malaysian companies including Petronas unit Gentari, UMW Group and Salcon Bhd.
Indian companies, meanwhile, had 293 approved manufacturing projects in Malaysia worth US$2.95 billion as of June 2026, including joint ventures with Malaysian companies.
The projects are expected to create 28,455 jobs, Sharifah told reporters at a press conference here today.
The growing investment links complement expanding cooperation between the two countries in food security, transportation, the digital economy, defence, higher education, renewable energy and workforce management.
Malaysia's total trade with India, however, fell 5.0  per cent to RM79.33 billion (US$18.55 billion) in 2025 from RM83.5 billion (US$18.25 billion) in 2024, mainly due to a sharp decline in imports.
Malaysia's exports to India edged up 0.4 per cent to RM52.35 billion (US$12.25 billion) from RM52.13 billion (US$11.4 billion) in 2024, supported largely by higher shipments of non-metallic mineral products.
Exports of non-metallic mineral products surged RM1.20 billion, or 189.1%, last year, helping offset weaker performance in other trade segments.
Imports from India, meanwhile, fell 14 per cent to RM26.98 billion (US$6.29 billion) from RM31.37 billion (US$6.85 billion), mainly due to a RM4.23 billion, or 43.8 per cent, decline in petroleum product imports.
As a result, Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM25.37 billion with India in 2025, reinforcing its position as a net exporter in the bilateral relationship.
Sharifah Ezneeda said Malaysia's participation in BRICS would further extend its economic and diplomatic reach into major emerging markets, providing opportunities to expand trade and investment while strengthening cooperation in technology, energy, food security and digital transformation.
Malaysia, currently a BRICS partner country, is using the platform to deepen engagement with the grouping as it works towards full membership.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to use the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit to advance Malaysia's vision of a more inclusive and equitable international system and strengthen the voice of the Global South.
During the summit, Anwar is scheduled to deliver Malaysia's National Statement, "Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth", calling for stronger cooperation among BRICS member and partner countries to address development challenges, widen economic opportunities and ensure the benefits of technological advancement and innovation are more broadly shared.
The summit, the highest-level BRICS platform, brings together heads of state and government from member and partner countries to discuss global governance, sustainable development, economic cooperation, trade and investment, digital transformation and challenges facing developing economies.
Anchored in the "Humanity First" framework, Malaysia's position is aligned with key BRICS priorities including economic resilience, digital transformation and sustainable development.
The grouping represents a substantial economic opportunity, with a combined market of 3.88 billion people and gross domestic product of US$29.85 trillion, equivalent to 27.1 per cent of global GDP.
Sharifah Ezneeda said Malaysia's BRICS participation also complements its engagement in multilateral platforms including Asean, the United Nations and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, while broadening its diplomatic and economic networks with major emerging economies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Toddler dies after being found unconscious at babysitter's home in Air Itam
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 1-year-old toddler died after being found unconscious at a babysitter's home in Kampung Melayu, Air Itam, on Tuesday.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report from the Penang Hospital Emergency and Trauma Department at 5.16pm on Sept 8 concerning the child's death.
He said the 13-month-old Sabah-born indigenous child was found unconscious with bluish lips by the 44-year-old babysitter around 2pm.
"The child was taken to Penang Hospital by the mother and babysitter after being found unconscious," he said in a statement.
Rozak said the child arrived at the hospital at 2.45pm and was pronounced dead at 3.33pm following emergency treatment.
"Police have detained the babysitter and the child's mother to assist investigations," he said.
A post-mortem was conducted yesterday, but the cause of death remains pending laboratory analysis.
The case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
"The babysitter was remanded for seven days from Sept 9 to 15, while the mother was remanded for three days from Sept 9 to 11 to assist investigations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian woman dies in Perth after alleged domestic assault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 28-year-old Malaysian woman residing in Perth, Australia, has died after allegedly being assaulted late last month.
Tan Kah Ming was found unresponsive at a residence on Taree Street, St James, at 8.30pm on Aug 26, according to a 7News Australia report on Aug 28.
She was rushed to Royal Perth Hospital but died shortly after arrival.
Homicide detectives allege that Younis Qambari, 38, inflicted extensive injuries on Tan during an assault in the days preceding her death.
Police allege the offence occurred within the context of a domestic relationship.
Qambari was charged with murder on Aug 28 and appeared briefly before the Perth magistrate's court.
Bail was not considered, and he was remanded in custody to appear in court later this month.
Meanwhile, 7News reported that Tan's sister, who lived nearby, was distraught over the tragedy and trying to come to terms with the loss.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Give us space to lead today,' says Puteri Umno chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Puteri Umno wants greater leadership opportunities now rather than being treated merely as the party's future, said its chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi.
She called on Umno's top leadership to give young women in the movement greater space, trust and responsibility to prove their ability to lead.
"If Puteri is the future, give us space to lead today. Listen to our voices, give us space, give us trust and give us responsibility.
"We are not asking for space because we are young.
"We are asking for space because we are ready, ready to carry the responsibility and ready to prove our ability," she said in her winding-up speech at the Puteri Umno delegates' meeting here today.
Nurul Amal said Puteri members should not have to wait for future opportunities before taking on leadership responsibilities.
She said the movement's priority should be to move beyond slogans and programmes by delivering practical solutions and measurable results for the people.
"We must move from slogans to solutions, from programmes to impact, from promises to proof, and from a generation that waits to a generation that leads," she said.
Nurul Amal said the 25th anniversary of Puteri Umno should also be seen as an opportunity to prepare the next generation by setting an example for younger members.
She urged Puteri leaders at branch and state levels to ensure the movement remained a platform where young women could develop their leadership skills and take on greater responsibilities.
She said the movement's future depended not on waiting for its turn, but on being prepared to lead when opportunities arose.
"The future does not wait for us. We are the ones who must lead the future," she said.
Nurul Amal also reminded members that Puteri's role extended beyond preserving the movement's legacy, as they were also responsible for shaping its next chapter.
"Twenty-five years ago, we built history. For the next 25 years, we must create the history of the future.
"Puteri is not merely the future. Puteri is the strength of today. Puteri is the future we are building now," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Domestic violence must be taken seriously, says deputy minister
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Domestic violence must never be normalised, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said, urging victims to seek help and protection and calling on society to remain vigilant against abuse.
Lim expressed sadness over the death of Malaysian Tan Kah Ming, who was reportedly found unresponsive in Perth, Australia, in an incident believed to be linked to domestic violence.
She extended her condolences to Tan's family and loved ones, particularly her children and family members coping with the loss.
"Domestic violence is not a private matter that should be hidden or endured alone. It is a serious form of violence and must never be normalised under any circumstances," she said.
She said domestic violence could have profound effects on victims, their children, families and the wider community.
Lim urged victims not to suffer in silence and to seek immediate assistance from trusted individuals or appropriate support services.
In Malaysia, Talian Kasih 15999 and WhatsApp 019-261 5999 operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, providing assistance, counselling, support and referrals to relevant services.
She also called on family members, friends, neighbours and the public to take signs of domestic violence seriously and provide support without judgement, while prioritising victims' safety.
Lim said the ministry would continue strengthening prevention, protection and support measures for victims and affected families.
She said the Domestic Violence Act 1994 (Act 521) provided a framework for protecting victims, including through protection orders and temporary placement in safe locations, subject to the law.
On the Perth case, Lim said she respected the investigation and actions of the Australian authorities.
She also called for Tan's family to be given privacy as they mourned their loss.
"May her family be granted strength and fortitude, and may they receive the justice they deserve," she said.
It was reported that a woman from Penang was allegedly killed in a domestic violence incident in Perth, Australia, last month.
According to 7NEWS Australia, Tan, 28, was found unresponsive at a residence on Taree Street in St James at 8.30pm on Aug 26.
She was rushed to Royal Perth Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar's India visit to boost trade, investment ties with key partner
Article:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's five-day working visit to India from Sept 11 to 15 is set to strengthen Malaysia's economic engagement with one of its key trading partners, with trade, investment and access to new markets high on the agenda.
Anwar will be in New Delhi until Sept 13 before travelling to Keralam later that day.
Deputy High Commissioner and Chargé d'Affaires at the Malaysian High Commission here, Sharifah Ezneeda Wafa, said Anwar is accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and a Malaysian business delegation.
She said the visit will feature high-level bilateral talks, business engagements and Malaysia's participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
The summit, themed "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Security", allows Malaysia to engage emerging economies and diversify trade partnerships.
Anwar will meet Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sept 12 to explore trade and investment opportunities, alongside separate meetings with business leaders.
He is also scheduled to hold bilateral talks with the presidents of Russia, Iran and Kazakhstan, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, and the director-general of the World Trade Organisation.
The programme also includes sideline bilateral meetings, providing further opportunities to advance Malaysia's economic and diplomatic interests with emerging markets and international institutions.
At a joint press conference in Putrajaya on Feb 8, Anwar called for Malaysia and India to look beyond past achievements and expand trade past the RM79.6 billion recorded in 2025.
Last year, Malaysia exported RM52.3 billion worth of goods to India, led by palm oil, palm-based agricultural products, and electrical and electronic products.
Imports from India totalled RM27.19 billion, comprising mainly agricultural products, petroleum products and chemicals.
Sharifah added that India remains Malaysia's largest trading partner in South Asia, making efforts to deepen commercial ties particularly significant as both countries seek to expand market access, investment flows and business opportunities.
On Sept 13, Anwar will attend the BRICS Leaders' Summit at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, joining member country leaders and outreach invitees.
BRICS, an expanding grouping of major emerging economies, is seeking to strengthen cooperation in areas including trade, investment and development.
Malaysia became a BRICS partner country in 2025 after applying to join the grouping.
She said the summit is also expected to provide opportunities for Malaysia to pursue stronger trade and investment links with emerging economies while expanding commercial ties with major markets beyond its traditional partners.
In Keralam, Anwar will meet Grand Mufti of India Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad on Sept 13 to exchange views on community development, education and religious affairs.
He will also meet Keralam Governor Thiru Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar and local business leaders to discuss opportunities in education, investment and connectivity.
The Keralam engagements are expected to provide another avenue for Malaysia to deepen commercial links with the Indian state, particularly in investment, education and connectivity, as both sides seek to expand economic cooperation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia ranks second in Asean digital nations index
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia ranked second among Asean countries in the GSMA's 2026 Digital Nations Index, behind Singapore.
The index highlighted the country's digital infrastructure, data governance, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence (AI) policies.
Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines were also among the countries showing progress in the index, according to the GSMA's Digital Nations Asean 2026 report released on Thursday, the closing day of M360 Asean 2026 here.
The report's findings come as policymakers, regulators and industry representatives discussed regional digital integration at the three-day event.
GSMA director-general Vivek Badrinath said Asean's target of building a US$2 trillion digital economy by 2030 would require greater coordination between national digital strategies.
"The foundations have been built, and Asean has set itself a bold ambition: a US$2 trillion digital economy by 2030," he said.
"What's clear is that ambition must now translate into action, connecting national strategies into a more integrated, interoperable regional digital economy."
He said governments, mobile operators and digital platforms would all have a role in advancing regional digital integration.
The final day of M360 Asean 2026 focused on connecting national digital strategies and developing a more integrated regional digital market as digital services become more widely adopted across Asean.
Speakers included Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching, Axiata Group Bhd group chief executive officer Nik Rizal Kamil, Globe Telecom president and CEO Carl Cruz, Vodafone president for Asia Bhupinder Singh and Sri Lanka President's chief adviser Dr Hans Wijayasuriya.
Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil, Asean secretary-general Dr Kao Kim Hourn and Badrinath delivered opening remarks at the event.
The GSMA will next convene the global mobile industry at MWC26 Doha, scheduled for Nov 8-10,
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bermaz Auto's Q1 earnings surge to RM40.5mil, revenue rises to RM553mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bermaz Auto Bhd's net profit jumped multifold to RM40.5 million in the first quarter of financial year 2026 (Q1 FY26) from RM8.28 million a year earlier, due to higher sales volume from its Mazda domestic operations.
Bermaz Auto's revenue rose 12.6 per cent to RM553 million in the quarter ended July 31, 2026, from RM491 million last year.
Bermaz Auto declared a dividend of two sen per share, payable on Nov 4.
In a statement, the company said the better performance was driven mainly by higher sales volume from its Mazda domestic operations, particularly the Mazda3, which continued to receive a favourable response from consumers.
This was partly offset by lower sales volume from its Kia domestic operations following the cessation of its distributorship in November 2025.
The company said inflationary pressures, geopolitical uncertainties and weaker global growth could continue to weigh on the Malaysian economy.
The influx of Chinese-brand vehicles and aggressive pricing have also led to excess inventory and continued discounting in the automotive market.
"The company managed to cushion the impact with the launching of new completely built-up (CBU) models such as the Mazda3 and the Xpeng G6 and X9, which were well received by consumers.
"Upcoming models to be launched are the new CBU Mazda CX5 2.5G and the CBU Mazda CX-80 3.3G mild hybrid electric vehicles, which the company envisagess will be well-received by consumers.
"Having considered the above, the board is cautious of the changing environment but remains positive that the company will maintain its competitive position and profitability for the financial year ending April 30, 2027," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Respect Malay Rulers despite political differences, says Puteri Umno
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan has been urged not to challenge or question the authority of the Malay Rulers, particularly over the power of pardon, for the sake of political differences.
A Puteri Umno delegate Nur Atiqah Othman said differences of opinion and political competition were part of democracy, but the limits of respect for the institution that served as the country's constitutional pillar must not be crossed.
"We can have different opinions and political views, debate and compete in elections, but when it comes to the royal institution, we must maintain respect and observe the boundaries.
"Political differences should never become a reason to question the institution that serves as the nation's umbrella. Umno will continue to defend the sovereignty of the Malay Rulers and the principles of constitutional monarchy," she said while debating the Puteri Umno chief's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Nur Atiqah, who is also Kedah Puteri Umno deputy chief, also conveyed her candid concerns to the party leadership over the dynamics of relations within the unity government.
She urged political partners to engage in genuine cooperation rather than simply making promises on stage.
She said some proposals and plans drawn up by Umno had received no response from its coalition partners.
"The party machinery is sidelined, meetings are not called and discussions are forgotten. Remember, we are the ones who campaign on the ground. We are the ones who face voters' questions and complaints.
"Therefore, the voices and sentiments of the grassroots must be heard. Never make political decisions that disregard the spirit of those working at the grassroots," she said.
On calls from some quarters for unity with other political parties, Nur Atiqah said Puteri Umno respected those views but stressed that the party must not forget the lessons of its past experiences.
"In politics, we can adjust our strategy, but Umno's principles, dignity and identity must never be sacrificed," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FDS heli crash: Remains to be released after DNA identification
Article:
MIRI: The remains of all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash will be handed over to their families once DNA identification results are obtained.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said post-mortems on the five victims were still being conducted at Miri Hospital following Tuesday's crash in Long Lellang.
He said the remains would only be released to the next of kin after the DNA identification process was completed.
"Post-mortems have not been completed. The remains will be handed over to the victims' families once the DNA test results are obtained," he said when contacted.
The DNA identification process is necessary to confirm the identities of all the victims before their remains are released to their respective families.
The DNA tests, conducted by the Chemistry Department, are expected to take another one to two days.
The five victims were identified as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin and medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry.
Also killed in the crash were nurses Debra Moset and Jessie Paya Jok
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar briefs Sultan of Selangor on state development
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today had an audience with the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, to brief the ruler on state development matters.
"During the meeting, I briefed His Royal Highness on several matters, including current issues involving the development of Selangor," Anwar said in a social media post today.
Anwar also wished His Royal Highness and the royal family continued blessings, good health, well-being and sovereignty.
The audience was among a series of engagements with the prime minister today.
Earlier, Anwar also met with
Kelantan Menteri Besar
Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, with discussions focusing on the state's development and efforts to strengthen federal-state cooperation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lawyer claims Negri MB willingly signed proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN: A lawyer representing the dismissed Undang of Negri Sembilan; the Tunku Besar Tampin; and the Datuk Shahbandar, has claimed that Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim knowingly and willingly signed a proclamation to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Mohd Khairul Azam Abdul Aziz said Ismail's claim that he signed the proclamation against his will was an afterthought.
"The Menteri Besar's reason that he signed the proclamation under duress is an afterthought.
"There were no circumstances that occurred that night which could have led to any element of coercion against the Menteri Besar in making the decision," he said at a press conference at the Galeri Diraja Tuanku Jaafar here this afternoon.
Yesterday, Ismail, in a statement, said that the Instrument of Proclamation to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, which he signed on Aug 3 at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson, was signed "
against his will and under duress
."
He said he lodged a police report on Sept 8 to enable the authorities to conduct an investigation.
Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, maintained that the Negri Sembilan government was of the view that the Instrument did not comply with the processes and procedures stipulated under Article 10 of the Negri Sembilan
Constitution 1959.
He said it was therefore invalid, unconstitutional and unenforceable.
Elaborating on the events at Istana Laguna Biru on Aug 3, Mohd Khairul Azam said that at about 8pm, the Undang of Jelebu, Undang Johol, Undang Rembau, Tunku Besar Tampin and Datuk Shahbandar Sungei Ujong had gathered there for a dinner with Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar.
He said Ismail arrived at about 10pm, accompanied by his lawyer, Datuk Abu Bakar Isa Ramat.
"At that time, an audience was held between Datuk Ismail Lasim and Tuanku Nadzaruddin, the Undang of Jelebu, the Undang of Johol, the Undang of Rembau, the Tunku Besar of Tampin and the Datuk Shahbandar of Sungei Ujong.
"During the audience, all the Undang present, together with the Tunku Besar of Tampin, gave their blessing for Ismail's appointment as the ninth Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar and prayed that he and the new state leadership would be able to resolve the crisis involving the state's customary institutions," he said.
He said the Undang had explained to Ismail the decision by the Undang Yang Empat to dismiss Tuanku Muhriz through a Proclamation dated April 19, 2026, pursuant to Article 10(1) of the state constitution, in the presence of Ismail's lawyer.
He said Ismail was informed that the Instrument of Proclamation required the signature of the Menteri Besar under Article 10(1)(b) of the state constitution.
"After the reasons for the dismissal of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir were explained, Ismail agreed to sign the Proclamation for his dismissal in the presence of his lawyer.
"We maintain that the Menteri Besar signed the Proclamation dated Aug 3, 2026, voluntarily and without coercion, in the presence of his lawyer, who was with him throughout the event," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Puteri Umno urges respect for Pardons Board constitutional process
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Puteri Umno delegate has urged political parties "on the other side" not to pre-empt the constitutional process of the Pardons Board.
Melaka Puteri Umno deputy chief Nur Farhana Ab Ghani also urged the parties not to create political pressure or shape public perceptions before the process takes place.
"However, delegates, are we not surprised? When he received a pardon in 2018, the pardon mechanism was celebrated and respected.
"So today, the same principle should be respected regardless of who is involved. Puteri Umno is not asking anyone to determine the Pardons Board's decision.
"We are only demanding one thing: respect the constitutional process and the institution of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong," she said while debating the Puteri Umno chief's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
It was reported that Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh confirmed that the Pardons Board would meet tomorrow, but
declined to commen
t on whether former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's application would be discussed.
Hannah was quoted as saying that she was among those called to attend the meeting at 8.30am, but declined to elaborate.
Najib is currently serving a prison sentence after being convicted in the SRC International case.
In 2024, the Pardons Board reduced Najib's 12-year prison sentence to six years and cut his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
Najib later claimed that there was an additional order from former Yang di-Pertuan Agong Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Meanwhile, Nur Farhana, who is also Kota Melaka Puteri Umno division chief, expressed disappointment over the treatment of party leaders as though they had already been convicted, despite no sentence having been imposed.
She said she was upset to see a party leader handcuffed, transported in a caged van and dressed in an orange prison uniform, which she said created the impression of guilt before a final verdict.
"Recently, delegates have been stirred by the issue of the Royal Commission of Inquiry report on Lembaga Tabung Haji. I do not think this is my area of expertise to speak at length about.
"However, I want to express my regret and disappointment that our leadership has been treated in this manner. Is that appropriate?
"The basic principle of law states that a person is innocent until proven guilty. But today, what we see is as though the punishment has already been imposed. We see pictures and headlines creating an initial perception that our leader is already guilty," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
