Title: 'Don't invent what PH didn't say,' Kamil tells Asyraf"
Article:
IPOH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) has never questioned the constitutional powers of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to grant pardons, said PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim.
He said claims that PH had disputed the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's powers under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution were based on a misinterpretation of the coalition's statement.
Muhammad Kamil said PH respected the Federal Constitution and the country's institutions while maintaining its position against corruption and abuse of power.
"I find Asyraf's reaction rather perplexing. Perhaps a careful reading of the PH statement would help, because nowhere in it did PH question, dispute or even touch upon the constitutional powers of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to grant pardons under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
"That simply was not in the statement," he said when contacted.
He was responding to Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, who criticised PH for allegedly questioning the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's constitutional powers to grant pardons.
Asyraf had also accused PH of applying a double standard, questioning why the coalition had supported the pardon granted to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim before he completed his full sentence, while adopting a different stance on others.
Muhammad Kamil said PH had also upheld the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's position that corruption cases must be investigated thoroughly and without compromise.
He said there was no contradiction between respecting the constitutional powers of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and PH's right to state its position on corruption, abuse of power and the rule of law.
"PH's position is straightforward. We respect the constitutional powers of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"At the same time, PH has every right and responsibility to its supporters and to Malaysians to state clearly its principled position on corruption, abuse of power and the rule of law," he said.
Muhammad Kamil said political leaders should respond to what was actually stated instead of attributing positions to PH that had never been expressed.
"It is important that we respond to what was actually said, rather than what we imagine was said," he said.
Muhammad Kamil said Asyraf, as a senior political leader, should exercise greater care when interpreting political statements before making accusations against PH.
"Don't conveniently drag PH into a controversy of Umno's own making. Read what we actually said. Don't invent what we didn't."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Just regular afternoon tea,' says Umno president's aide on Zahid-Negri MB meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The meeting between Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim ended after two hours.
It is learnt that the meeting was held following Ismail's claim that he was pressured into signing a
controversial proclamation
, after Zahid earlier said he wanted to meet Ismail and seek an explanation over the matter.
Among those who attended the meeting, which started at about 4pm at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, were Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and all three Umno vice-presidents, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
Johari was seen leaving the room where the meeting took place about an hour later.
About 40 minutes later, Khaled was seen leaving the room.
"It's tomorrow," Khaled said briefly when asked about the agenda and outcome of the meeting.
Zahid's political secretary Datuk Seri Megat Zulkarnain Omardin emerged from the room at about 6.20pm and told reporters waiting outside that it was just a "regular meeting over afternoon tea".
"No press conference. Everyone has already left the room.
"It was just a regular afternoon tea for all Umno leaders," he said.
The New Straits Times, however, spotted Ismail leaving the premises in an official Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar vehicle about 6.30pm
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC thanks RTD for cooperation in exposing vehicle ownership document syndicate
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has thanked the Road Transport Department (RTD) for its cooperation and intelligence-sharing, which helped expose a syndicate allegedly falsifying documents to facilitate vehicle ownership transfers in Perak.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said cooperation between the two enforcement agencies was instrumental in uncovering the syndicate's activities.
"We would like to express our appreciation to the RTD for the cooperation and support extended to the MACC in this case.
"This is the kind of cooperation that we need between enforcement agencies, particularly in information and intelligence-sharing to uncover wrongdoing and ensure those involved are brought to justice," he said.
The operation resulted in the arrest of 11 people, comprising six civil servants and five people in Perak on Tuesday night.
The seven men and four women, aged between their 20s and 40s, were arrested at about 10pm after turning up to give their statements at the Perak MACC office.
They are being remanded until Sept 14 to facilitate investigations.
The syndicate is suspected of falsifying vehicle ownership documents and bribing enforcement agency officers in Perak to facilitate changes to vehicle ownership status.
The syndicate was uncovered following six months of intelligence-sharing between the MACC and RTD.
Abd Halim said the case demonstrated the importance of close cooperation between government enforcement agencies in detecting corruption and other forms of misconduct.
He said such collaboration would continue to be strengthened to safeguard the integrity of government services and prevent systems and procedures from being exploited by unscrupulous parties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Guan Eng trial: Penang mayor to testify on Sept 28
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Penang mayor Datuk Rajendran Anthony will be called as a prosecution witness in the corruption trial involving former Penang chief minister Lim Guan Eng over the state's major roads and undersea tunnel project.
Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin told the Sessions Court here today that the prosecution would call Rajendran to testify on Sept 28.
He said the defence had previously agreed for Rajendran's witness statement to be deemed read or tendered in court without the witness having to read it aloud during the trial.
However, Guan Eng's lawyer Ram Karpal Singh said the defence had yet to decide whether Rajendran's statement would be deemed read or whether the witness would read it in court.
"Not necessarily, Your Honour. We will examine the matter," he said.
Rajendran was Penang City Council Engineering Department director when the undersea tunnel project was proposed in 2011, and was also involved in early discussions with Consortium Zenith BUCG Sdn Bhd on the preparation of the request for proposal (RFP) documents for the tunnel project.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigating officer Senior Superintendent Zulhilmi Ramli, 34, agreed with the defence's suggestion that Beijing Urban Construction Group (BUCG) scored the highest mark of 93 per cent in the RFP for the tunnel project.
The 38th prosecution witness also agreed that the company's technical and financial capabilities were among the factors considered in the scoring process.
However, Zulhilmi said he was not a member of the committee that conducted the evaluation, but that the scoring process was among the matters he investigated as the investigating officer.
When questioned about the RFP process, Zulhilmi said eight companies were shortlisted at the initial stage before 4 were invited to participate in the RFP, based on assessments of technical and financial criteria.
"The selection of the four companies was based on technical and financial criteria assessed by the relevant committee," he said.
The witness also agreed that the RFP process took about a year to conclude, with several parties, including the Penang state government, state financial officers and local authorities, involved in the process.
He also agreed with Ram Karpal's suggestion that there were five key criteria considered by the technical committee in awarding BUCG high marks.
The criteria were BUCG's satisfactory technical experience, sufficient financial capability, its proposal for the project in the RFP, the lower cost proposed and savings.
Ram: That was one of the factors considered by the committee in selecting BUCG, correct?
Witness: Correct.
Ram: Fourth, the company proposed a reasonable concession, namely the shortest toll concession period of only 30 years, correct?
Witness: Correct.
Ram: Fifth, BUCG obtained the lowest land approval, correct?
Witness: Correct.
During re-examination, Zulhilmi maintained that his investigation found that Guan Eng had "promised" to award the tunnel project to former Consortium Zenith Construction Sdn Bhd (CZCSB) director Datuk Zarul Ahmad Mohd Zulkifli through direct negotiations.
The trial before Judge Azura Alwi resumes on Sept 28.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AME Elite buys Pontian land for RM200mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AME Elite Consortium Bhd is acquiring 71.43 hectares of freehold land in Pontian, Johor for RM199.8 million cash.
The land, located in Jeram Batu within the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), is connected to the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link Expressway.
The industrial space solutions provider said the acquisition will strengthen its Johor development footprint.
It will also position the group to capture rising demand from investors and manufacturers seeking integrated industrial space within the JS-SEZ.
AME Elite executive director and group chief executive officer Dylan Tan Teck Eng said the acquisition would enable the group to capitalise on growing foreign and domestic direct investment flows into Johor.
"While we have broadened our presence into three key economic regions in Peninsular Malaysia, Johor remains the heartbeat of our expansion strategy.
"Through our integrated development model with specialised construction and engineering expertise, we continue to transform untapped strategic land into higher-value industrial ecosystems," he said in a statement.
The acquisition will be funded through internally generated funds, with the sale and purchase agreements entered into by AME Elite's subsidiaries Pulai Land West Sdn Bhd and Pulai Land East Sdn Bhd.
Completion is targeted for the first half of 2027.
The acquisition follows a separate 12.9-hectare land deal in Senai announced in March, involving a total cash consideration of RM101.2 million.
Together, the two acquisitions will add more than 80.9 hectares to the company's remaining 119.5-hectare land bank as it expands across Johor, Penang and Selangor.
AME Elite said demand for integrated industrial space remained robust, with its flagship developments.
This includes i-Park@Indahpura, i-Park@Senai Airport City and i-TechValley at SILC, recording strong take-up.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak dominates unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 183
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Serian recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 183 as of 5.30pm today, with 11 areas nationwide recording unhealthy air quality.
Checks on the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Sarawak recording the highest readings, with Sarikei at 182, followed by Samarahan (176), Kuching (175), Samalaju (165), Sri Aman (157), Sibu (155) and Mukah (154).
In the peninsula, Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur recorded 167, while Larkin (119) and Pasir Gudang (112) in Johor were also in the unhealthy range.
Another 52 areas recorded moderate air quality, with Johor registering some of the highest readings — Kota Tinggi (95), Pengerang (93), Kluang (92), Batu Pahat (90) and Tangkak (88).
In Sabah, Kimanis recorded 91, followed by Kota Kinabalu (90), Labuan (84), Tawau (77), Sandakan (60) and Keningau (57).
Several areas in Sarawak also recorded moderate readings, including Bintulu (86), Miri (83), ILP Miri (79), Kapit (74) and Limbang (71).
Within the Klang Valley, Johan Setia recorded the highest reading in Selangor at 87, followed by Cheras, Kuala Lumpur (85), Shah Alam (74), Petaling Jaya (71), Banting (69) and Kuala Selangor (67).
In Perak, Ipoh recorded 92, followed by Seri Manjung (80), Tanjung Malim (74), Pegoh Ipoh (70) and Taiping (66).
On the east coast, Kuala Terengganu recorded 86, followed by Kuantan (85), Indera Mahkota (80), Kemaman (80), Rompin (78), Paka (77), Jerantut (76), Besut (72), Tanah Merah (66), Temerloh (65) and Kota Baru (64).
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai improved to a moderate reading of 85 after recording an unhealthy 104 earlier today. Alor Gajah recorded 84, while Bandaraya Melaka stood at 71.
Nilai and Seremban in Negri Sembilan both recorded 76, while Port Dickson stood at 70.
Up north, Sungai Petani recorded 59, while Seberang Jaya in Penang stood at 55, followed by Seberang Perai (53) and Minden (52).
Five areas recorded good air quality — Kulim Hi-Tech (47), Alor Star (43), Balik Pulau (34), Kangar, Perlis (30) and Langkawi (30).
Yesterday morning, Serian recorded a very unhealthy API reading of 212 amid persistent hotspot activity in Kalimantan and Sumatra.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
The public can obtain the latest hourly API readings via the DOE website or the MyJAS EQMS mobile application.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New Hoong Fatt to park RM20mil in venture fund
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: New Hoong Fatt Holdings Bhd's unit Jhi Soon Manufacturing Industries Sdn Bhd plans to invest up to RM20 million in a venture capital fund established.
It will be set up through a special purpose venture capital fund vehicle Cypress Drive Ventures Sdn Bhd (FundCo).
Jhi Soon will subscribe to up to 20 million class A redeemable preference shares in FundCo at RM1 per share.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the investment forms part of the capital allocation strategy, providing the group access to a diversified portfolio of early-stage and high-growth investment opportunities.
"The proposed investment also enables the group to participate in potential long-term capital appreciation and investment returns, while benefiting from the fund manager's expertise in sourcing, evaluating and managing venture capital investments," it said.
The investment will be funded internally and drawn down progressively through capital calls.
The fund will be managed by Cypress Asia Sdn Bhd for seven years from the date of the agreement, with an option to extend for up to two successive 12-month periods.
The investment committee will comprise two members nominated by New Hoong Fatt and two nominated by the fund promoter Cypress Asia Capital Sdn Bhd.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry van, bus collide on Senai-Desaru Expressway
Article:
KULAI: A Health Ministry van carrying one passenger and a bus were involved in a collision at KM23.3 of the Senai-Desaru Expressway (southbound) near here today.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee, who confirmed the incident, said no one was injured in the 12.30pm accident.
"Both parties have lodged police reports.
"The bus was not carrying any passengers, while the Health Ministry van had one passenger on board. No injuries were reported," he said.
Tan said the case was being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for careless and inconsiderate driving.
Meanwhile, Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the staff involved in the incident were safe.
"The staff are all okay," he said.
The New Straits Times learnt that the van was ferrying patient samples from Enche' Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital in Kluang to Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Baru when the accident occurred.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azeez released from police custody, lawyer says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has been released from police custody, his lawyer said.
Counsel Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad said the former Baling member of Parliament was freed earlier this afternoon and had proceeded to attend the Umno general assembly.
Azeez is a member of Umno's supreme council.
Amer said Azeez had expressed relief upon his release after two days at the Dang Wangi police station.
"I have been informed that he was released around 3pm. He is relieved to be out and in good spirits," he told the New Straits Times.
Azeez was yesterday charged with using his position to secure the position of chairman of a company with an annual remuneration of RM690,000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM Anwar to meet Modi, Putin and other leaders during Brics Summit in New Delhi
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is set to engage in high-level bilateral meetings with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to the Indian capital for the 18th Brics Summit this weekend.
“Besides Modi and Putin, the Prime Minister will also meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on the sidelines of the Summit.
“These are confirmed bilateral meetings; there could be more provided both parties can agree on the timing,” Malaysia’s Chargé d’Affaires, Deputy High Commissioner, Sharifah Ezneeda Wafa told Malaysian media ahead of the Prime Minister’s arrival on Sept 11 here.
Malaysia is participating in the Brics Leaders’ Summit in New Delhi as a Brics Partner Country.
Hosted by Modi, the Summit carries the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with a focus on strengthening resilience, economic cooperation as well as trade and investment reforms.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, will be accompanied by the Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and the Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan. — Bernama

Title: Three suspects arrested in Alam Megah murder case, police thank public for vital leads
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have arrested three of seven suspects wanted to assist investigations into the Alam Megah murder in Section 28, here last month.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the suspects, all locals in their 20s and 40s, were arrested between Sept 4 and 7 following leads from members of the public after their photographs were made public last Friday.
“For the case which involves Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Penal Code, we have received instructions to charge the three suspects arrested recently, while the remaining four wanted individuals are still being hunted.
“The police would like to express our appreciation to members of the public and the media for their assistance, which led to the arrests,” he said in a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) here today.
He said on a separate case being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting in Taman Sri Muda here on Aug 13, no new arrest had been made so far.
On Aug 27, Shazeli said a brawl involving a group of individuals that resulted in the death of a man in Taman Alam Megah was believed to have stemmed from hostility and turf war between two secret societies.
Meanwhile, commenting on public calls for the proposed construction of a new police station in Puncak Alam following three successful operations to dismantle drug laboratories in the area, Shazeli said there are several key factors that need to be taken into consideration.
He said the establishment of a new police station does not depend solely on the discovery or exposure of drug laboratories in an area.
“The construction of a new police station is subject to consideration of various important criteria, such as population density, the pace of economic activity, and overall crime trends in the area.
“Although the area is large, population density in some parts is not yet widespread, and rushing to construct a new police station could reduce the efficiency of police manpower distribution,” he said.
He said the police, through the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) and patrol squads, have proactively stepped up patrols and security measures throughout the area to curb criminal activities. — Bernama

Title: Op Fella widens: MACC wants prison access to question ex‑Felda chairman on asset deals
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will seek the cooperation of the Malaysian Prison Department to record the statement of a former Felda chairman currently serving a prison sentence to assist its investigation into the assets and investments of Felda Investment Corporation (FIC).
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the statement needed to be recorded due to a link between the purchase of certain assets and FIC investments currently under investigation.
“We are in the process. We might make the request next week. There are procedures that must be followed,” he said at a press conference at the MACC headquarters here today.
Abd Halim said seven investigation papers had been opened to date under ‘Op Fella’, while statements from 29 witnesses had been recorded in investigations into alleged corruption involving asset purchases and investments by Felda and FIC.
He said the witnesses included former members of the Felda and FIC Boards of Directors, management personnel from both entities, as well as individuals from government agencies and the private sector.
“Among those who have been summoned are former members of the Felda and FIC boards of directors, management personnel from Felda and FIC, as well as representatives from other entities such as land authorities, independent valuers, law firms, and others.
“All the witnesses are interconnected,” he said.
On Sept 6, the MACC detained two individuals linked to the investigation — a former Felda director-general and a former FIC chief executive officer — who remain under remand to assist in the investigation.
Abd Halim said the MACC was also tracing the flow of funds to determine whether there had been any misconduct or bribery involving FIC officials.
“The investigation is ongoing, focusing on documents related to a purchase in Sarawak, the acquisition of an overseas hotel and the establishment of Felda’s own subsidiaries,” he said.
In a related development, he said the MACC was also investigating allegations of misappropriation and abuse of power involving Felda Palong 7 in Negeri Sembilan.
He said statements had so far been recorded from eight individuals, comprising five Felda witnesses and three suppliers.
“The MACC is seeking the cooperation of the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) to verify the specifications of the supplied seedlings,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Judges Alice Loke and Elaine Yap take oaths, marking new appointments in Malaysian judiciary
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — High Court Judge Alice Loke Yee Ching today took her oath of office and allegiance as a Court of Appeal judge.
Judicial Commissioner Elaine Yap Chin Gaik, meanwhile, took her oath of office and allegiance as a High Court judge.
Loke took her oath before Court of Appeal President Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, while Yap took hers before Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah.
Also present at the swearing-in ceremony were Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh and Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi.
Loke, 64, who hails from Taiping, Perak, is formerly the head of the Civil Division at the Attorney General’s Chambers. She was appointed a High Court Judicial Commissioner on July 10, 2020.
As a Kuala Lumpur High Court judge in the Special Powers Division, Loke presided over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s judicial review application concerning an alleged addendum order that would have allowed him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Meanwhile, Yap, 53, who hails from Penang, was appointed a High Court Judicial Commissioner on Aug 28, 2024, and confirmed as a High Court judge on Nov 3, 2025.
Prior to her appointment as a Judicial Commissioner, she was the sole proprietor of the law firm Elaine Yap Law Office. She currently serves in the Commercial Division of the Kuala Lumpur High Court.
Both appointments take effect today. — Bernama

Title: Super El Niño to torch Malaysia next March, MetMalaysia warns heat soaring past 40°C
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) expects temperatures in several parts of the country to exceed 40 degrees Celsius next year, driven by a Super El Niño phenomenon forecast to reach its strongest intensity on record.
MetMalaysia director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the phenomenon’s impact would typically begin to be felt towards the end of the Northeast Monsoon, particularly in the northern states of the Peninsula.
He added that the peak of the extreme heat was expected to coincide with the equinox period around March to April next year, further driving temperatures to extreme levels.
“The highest daily temperature ever recorded in the country was 40.1 degrees Celsius in Chuping, Perlis, during the Super El Niño phenomenon of 1997/1998.
“Given that this phenomenon is forecast to be stronger than previous episodes, compounded by global warming, temperatures can surpass that record and reach 40.5 or even 41 degrees Celsius,” he said during an appearance on Bernama Radio’s Fokus 30 programme titled Super El Niño: Kesan Kepada Negara (Super El Niño: Impact on the Nation), today.
He added that Muslims are expected to fast and celebrate Hari Raya in very hot weather next year, and that visiting and outdoor pursuits should therefore be avoided for the sake of safety and health.
“The sun is directly overhead during the equinox, and without sufficient cloud cover due to the dry weather, direct exposure to heat can have adverse effects,” he cautioned.
Mohd Hisham said the current weather environment was still at the ordinary El Niño stage and would have to pass gradually through the weak, moderate and strong phases before developing into a very strong or Super El Niño by the end of this year.
He said Malaysia had faced three Super El Niño events before, in 1982/1983, 1997/1998 and 2015/2016, during which the country’s daily weather became extremely hot.
Mohd Hisham said the Super El Niño phenomenon generally occurs due to rising sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, which influence global atmospheric conditions, causing a significant reduction in rainfall and very dry weather, as well as raising the risk of high-intensity haze from open burning.
“Based on records, we have experienced continuous dry spells of up to 70 days in northern areas such as Langkawi and Alor Setar. This time, the phenomenon could cause a similarly prolonged dry spell,” he said, while also advising the public to make early preparations.
He therefore warned of the potential for a more serious water supply crisis next year, following the peak impact of the natural phenomenon.
This is because a significant delay in rainfall due to prolonged dry weather risks further depleting dam levels in several states that are already experiencing water supply disruptions.
“We are worried that when the peak of the Super El Niño arrives early next year, the situation will become more severe. Our experience during previous strong Super El Niño episodes saw dams in Melaka dry up completely,” he said.
Mohd Hisham also advised the public to always refer to valid weather information through official websites or MetMalaysia’s myCuaca app, and not to spread unverified information on social media. — Bernama

Title: MACC to charge ex‑minister Monday over Tabung Haji RCI, probe assets in Saudi Arabia
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — A former minister will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court next Monday as part of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) probe arising from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the commission had recommended three charges against the individual under Section 403 of the Penal Code for dishonest misappropriation of property.
Speaking at a special press conference at the MACC headquarters today, Abd Halim said the former minister was also linked to assets in Saudi Arabia.
He said five people had been charged so far in the TH RCI probe: a former deputy general manager of construction and a former security and health manager at TH Properties Sdn Bhd, a former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman, Alam Maritim Sdn Bhd’s chief executive officer, and a former TH chief operating officer.
In addition, of the 14 investigation papers opened by the MACC previously, six have been completed, with two leading to charges while four others were classified as no further action (NFA).
He said the remaining eight investigation papers were MACC initiatives stemming from the findings of the TH RCI report, with the commission recommending investigations into investments found to be suspicious and unsatisfactory.
“So far, we have recommended three, including the one to be charged on Monday. The rest are still in progress because they involve foreign entities in Saudi Arabia and Singapore.
“It takes time because we have to go through the mutual legal assistance (MLA) process, obtain documents from overseas parties and record statements,” he explained.
In a related development, Abd Halim denied claims that a senior Umno leader would be called to give evidence before the commission after the party’s general assembly next week.
It was previously reported in the media that another senior Umno leader was expected to be called by the MACC next week to assist in a case linked to the TH RCI report. — Bernama

Title: Police record 12 witness statements after RM2.91m armed gang robbery at Jalan Ampang condo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Police have recorded the statements of 12 witnesses to assist investigations into an armed gang robbery at a luxury condominium in Jalan Ampang here, involving losses of RM2.91 million.
In a statement today, Wangsa Maju police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said they are still working to identify all the suspects involved.
He added that the investigation would also examine any possibility or element of ‘insider’ involvement or collusion, given that the condominium has strict security controls.
He said that at the time of the robbery, the complainant had been inside the residence with eight other victims.
The media had previously reported that police were actively tracking down a group of masked men, in gloves and armed with knives, who broke into a residential unit at Pavilion Embassy between 2 pm and 3 pm on Sept 7.
The suspects made off with cash, jewellery and luxury watches estimated to be worth RM2.91 million, as well as damaging a mobile phone and stealing the passport of a 28-year-old Chinese national.
The case is being investigated under Sections 395/397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery and armed robbery.
Those with information on the incident are urged to contact the Wangsa Maju district police control centre at 03-9289 9222, Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Petronas-Petros deal could face ‘Tabung Haji’ reckoning in future, warns expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — A settlement between Petronas and Sarawak’s state-owned Petros could become a future accountability issue if it is seen as a political compromise rather than a decision made in the national interest, a former member of the MACC’s consultation and corruption prevention panel warned.
Walter Sandosam said the political circumstances surrounding any agreement could later come under scrutiny, even if it is defended today as a practical solution.
“Petronas-Petros could become a future accountability issue if a settlement is seen as political compromise rather than national-interest decision,” he said.
The warning comes ahead of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s meeting on the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) on Friday, where petroleum and revenue matters are expected to be among the key issues.
Petronas and Petros have been in talks over the Sarawak company’s role as the state gas aggregator, against a wider dispute over authority in the oil and gas sector.
Petros has cited Sarawak’s Distribution of Gas Ordinance 2016 in asserting its role in the state, while Petronas maintains that the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (PDA) gives it exclusive rights over the country’s petroleum resources.
Sandosam who is also the former president of the Institute of Internal Auditors Malaysia (IIAM) said the political context had changed, with the federal government now more dependent on Sabah and Sarawak.
“This creates space for political horse-trading,” he said.
He said giving Petros greater leeway over the aggregator issue could later be framed as a decision that weakened Petronas and the federal government’s position.
Sandosam said decision-makers should be mindful of the experience of Tabung Haji and Felda, where decisions made in a previous political climate were later revisited amid concerns over abuse of power, poor governance and oversight failures.
A royal commission of inquiry into Tabung Haji reprimanded executives over decisions influenced by political considerations, highlighting how actions taken by public institutions can be reassessed years later.
“Even good intentions or paper trails may not protect decision-makers later, because future opponents can still frame the deal as politically motivated,” Sandosam said.
He said the PDA should prevail if national interest was the main consideration.
Sandosam, who is also a former president of the Institute of Internal Auditors Malaysia, said any agreement must be assessed not only on the immediate political outcome but also on whether it protects the country’s long-term interests.
Petronas has repeatedly stressed that safeguarding national energy security is central to its role as Malaysia’s national oil company.
In its half-year results announcement last month, Petronas said its priority was to “safeguard energy security for those we serve”.
Its president and group CEO, Tengku Muhammad Taufik, said the company had strengthened its portfolio and worked across the value chain to deliver uninterrupted energy for Malaysia as its national oil company.

Title: Farmer shot dead outside family member’s rented house in Banting
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 10 — A 52-year-old local farmer was shot dead in front of a house believed to be occupied by his child in Teluk Bunut, Banting, on Tuesday.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the victim died at the scene after being hit by several shots in the incident between 10.30 pm and 11 pm.
“Police received information about the incident at about 11.15 pm. Investigations revealed that the premises was rented by the victim’s child and was unoccupied at the time.
“The victim is believed to have gone there to check on the house,” he told a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters here today.
Shazeli said the absence of independent witnesses and a weapon at the scene complicated the investigation, but the police had identified parties suspected to be linked to the incident.
Following the incident, police detained a local man in his 20s to 30s around the Banting area late last night.
“The man was brought to court today, and a two-day remand order was granted to assist in the investigation.
“The extent of this individual’s involvement, whether as the main suspect or otherwise, is still under scrutiny,” he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: No indication of volcanic ash entering Malaysian airspace, says MetMalaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — There are no indications that toxic volcanic ash from an eruption in Indonesia is moving across Malaysian airspace, as recently claimed on social media.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said current monitoring showed that volcanic ash, including from Gunung Anak Krakatau, was moving towards the Indian Ocean northwest of Sumatra, rather than towards Malaysia.
He said the volcano is also being closely monitored by an international monitoring centre in Darwin, Australia.
“The volcanic eruption or earthquake and the El Niño phenomenon affecting the country are two separate matters with no direct connection. They happened around the same period, which led some people to assume that they were related.
“Monitoring shows that the ash is moving towards open waters, not towards the peninsula, Sabah or Sarawak. I deny the viral claim and urge the public, especially keyboard warriors, to stop spreading unverified information to avoid causing panic,” he said when appearing as a guest on Fokus 30, a Bernama Radio programme titled ‘Super El Nino: Impact on the Country’ here today.
On current weather conditions, Mohd Hisham said the country was still experiencing a normal El Niño phase, which was gradually developing from weak to moderate and strong before potentially reaching a very strong or Super El Nino phase.
He said Super El Nino conditions were expected towards the end of the Northeast Monsoon, around March or April next year, particularly in the northern states of the peninsula.
Earlier, a social media post went viral claiming that sulphur dioxide from the latest eruption of Gunug Anak Krakatau in Indonesia had entered Malaysian airspace. The post featured red and orange atmospheric model images and urged the public to wear face masks.
Gunung Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait, previously experienced continuous eruptive activity for about 25 hours, beginning at 11.07pm on September 4 and ending at 12.04am on September 6. — Bernama

Title: Rosmah’s solar graft case: High Court to hear fresh evidence from key witness on Sept 17
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The High Court today set September 17 to hear additional evidence from the star prosecution witness, Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s solar hybrid project graft trial.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin fixed the date after Rosmah’s counsel, Datuk Jagjit Singh, told the court that the Court of Appeal had allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal and directed that the additional evidence be recorded by the High Court.
“I have to fix the dates because the order of the Court of Appeal is quite clear. I think we will fix the hearing dates in accordance with the order of the Court of Appeal until a stay is granted.
“If a stay is granted, then we will take it from there. If not, we will proceed as ordered by the Court of Appeal. If I don’t comply with the order, I will be in contempt of court,” Judge Aslam said before fixing September 17 for the hearing.
On September 1, the Court of Appeal allowed the wife of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence in the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project case.
The panel ordered that the additional evidence be obtained from Rayyan Radzwill, the 16th prosecution witness, through further cross-examination and re-examination.
Earlier, Jagjit said the Court of Appeal had already issued a specific order directing that case management be held today and requiring the High Court to record the additional evidence within two weeks.
“The Court of Appeal had also fixed the continuation of the criminal appeals for October, leaving a very tight timeline. The prosecution has filed a stay application, but no date has been fixed yet. We urge the court to proceed with fixing the dates,” he said.
Deputy public prosecutor Deepa Nair told the court that the prosecution had filed a notice of appeal on September 4 to the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal’s decision.
“We also filed an application to stay the Court of Appeal’s decision on September 8, and I have checked that there is no date yet. We have already put in a notice of urgency, so it’s not going to take much time.
“The matter will most probably be heard next week. Therefore, we seek for it to be adjourned pending the hearing of the stay application in the Court of Appeal,” she submitted.
She added that Rosmah’s appeal had been pending since 2022, and that the defence would not be prejudiced by a further postponement of a mere week or two.
Rosmah’s other counsel, Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader, objected to the adjournment, saying that the Court of Appeal had ordered that the matter be disposed of within two weeks.
“We only need one day. I handled the cross-examination at the High Court and will be doing so here as well,” he said.
Rosmah, 74, sought to adduce the additional evidence, consisting of a police report and a statutory declaration affirmed by Rayyan.
In the declaration, Rayyan allegedly claimed that he had been subjected to pressure from the prosecution during the trial.
On September 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah on three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and accepting RM6.5 million in bribes from Saidi Abang Samsudin, the former managing director of Jepak Holdings, through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The bribes were an inducement to help Jepak Holdings secure the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project for 369 rural schools in Sarawak from the Education Ministry.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment on each charge, to run concurrently, and was also fined RM970 million. She was subsequently granted a stay of execution pending the disposal of her appeal. — Bernama

Title: Four Chinese nationals face kidnapping charge after Singaporean allegedly held for RM3.28m ransom
Article:
BALIK PULAU, Sept 10 — Four Chinese nationals were charged at the Sessions Court here today with kidnapping a Singaporean man in July and demanding a ransom of SGD1 million (about RM3.28 million).
The accused, Liu Ting Jun, 46; Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 32; and Guan Siqi, 24, the only woman among them, however, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to them in Mandarin before Judge Ahzal Fariz Ahmad Khairuddin.
According to the charge sheet, the accused, as well as two others still at large and another two individuals who have since died, are accused of jointly abducting and wrongfully confining Quek Aik Teng at the Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas at 4.15 pm on July 26.
The charge is framed under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and caning, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Ikmal Affendi Zulkifly did not offer bail on the grounds that the case involved a serious offence and is a matter of public interest.
“A review of their passports is being carried out, and there is still no confirmation from the Immigration Department of Malaysia,” he said.
Counsel Azizul Hilmi Zulkifli, representing Guan, Huang and Wang, asked the court to consider bail with additional conditions, such as surrendering their passports, reporting to the nearest police station, and not interfering with prosecution witnesses.
Meanwhile, counsel Edward Ng, representing Liu, sought reasonable bail on the grounds that his client had cooperated with the police throughout the investigation and had no prior criminal record.
The judge dismissed all the bail applications and set Oct 15 for further mention of the case.
It was previously reported that police had shot dead two foreign nationals in Alor Setar, Kedah, last Saturday.
The suspects were believed to be members of a kidnapping syndicate that targeted foreign nationals, luring them with job offers and holiday packages after befriending them through dating apps and social media. — Bernama

Title: Drug syndicates use public as mules to smuggle cannabis to Europe, says Bukit Aman
Article:
BACHOK,  Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have found that drug trafficking syndicates operating by air to Europe frequently use members of the public as drug mules, particularly to transport cannabis flowers, which are in high demand on the continent.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department Director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said, however, that not all pilots arrested for involvement in drug smuggling were transporting drugs to Europe.
“As far as we know, only one or two pilots were involved. Among them was a co-pilot arrested in Jakarta, Indonesia.
“To our knowledge, he (the co-pilot) travelled to Australia and Indonesia, not Europe. Smuggling to Europe mostly involves drug mules from the general public,” he told reporters during a press conference following a strategic visit to the Bachok Narcotics Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen) today.
He said most air-based drug trafficking cases involving Europe centred on cannabis flowers due to the high demand for the illicit substance in the market.
He urged the public to be wary of offers from syndicates promising lucrative payments, including free flight tickets or holiday packages, or asking them to transport certain luggage overseas.
“Our citizens need to understand that it is unusual for someone to offer large sums of money to cover tickets, holiday packages and the like.
“So, do not get ensnared by these syndicates,” he said.
On how drug trafficking syndicates manage to bypass security controls at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Hussein said he could not elaborate as the Home Ministry is currently reviewing measures to strengthen security at all the country’s entry and exit points.
He said drug trafficking syndicates were becoming increasingly sophisticated and were exploiting various routes, including air, sea and land.
“If not by air, they use waterways, land routes and so on,” he said.
Hussein said that apart from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), PDRM had also recorded arrests linked to drug smuggling activities at Sultan Azlan Shah Airport in Ipoh.
Yesterday, Bernama reported that police had detained a man to assist in investigations into the drug-related arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta, Indonesia, last July.
The co-pilot was detained by Indonesian authorities at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs.
The Indonesian National Police (POLRI) subsequently found 15 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills and methamphetamine, with an estimated value of RM45 million. — Bernama

Title: Layang-Layang Aerospace voluntarily grounds BO-105 fleet after Sarawak helicopter crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd has voluntarily grounded its entire fleet of BO 105 helicopters and other aircraft powered by Rolls-Royce 250-series engines as a precautionary safety measure following the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Sarawak two days ago that claimed five lives.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the decision was taken by the operator voluntarily and should not be interpreted as an indication of technical failure.
“I wish to stress that this grounding is precautionary. It is a precautionary safety measure taken by the operator. It should not be interpreted as an indication that the engine or any other particular component caused the accident,” he told reporters at the Malaysia Aviation Safety Seminar (MASS) 2026, here today.
Norazman said CAAM records showed that the helicopter’s Certificate of Airworthiness was valid until Aug 4, 2027, while its Certificate of Registration remained valid until July 28, 2029.
Addressing concerns over the aircraft’s operational lifespan, he said age alone did not determine airworthiness as long as the aircraft was properly maintained and continued to meet all maintenance protocols.
“From an airworthiness perspective, age alone is not a determining factor, provided the aircraft is properly maintained in accordance with its approved maintenance program and continues to meet all applicable airworthiness requirements,” he said.
Norazman said CAAM was monitoring the operator’s grounding and inspection programme, while also verifying the relevant regulatory, operator and pilot records.
The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) under the Transport Ministry is independently investigating the crash.
“Any confirmed findings concerning the cause of the accident must come from AAIB following a thorough examination of the evidence. AAIB is responsible for establishing the circumstances, contributing factors, and cause of the accident...and CAAM is fully cooperating with the investigation and providing all relevant records,” he said.
Norazman urged the public and media to refrain from speculating on the cause of the crash before the investigation was completed.
“At this stage, it would be premature to speculate on whether the accident was caused by a technical issue, weather conditions, human factors, or any other factors,” he said.
On whether the operator had any previous history of air crashes, Norazman said CAAM would review its official records before releasing further details.
He added that in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 13 standards, AAIB would issue a preliminary investigation report within 30 days of the incident, followed by a final report within one year.
The BO-105 helicopter, operating a FDS mission, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching last Tuesday, killing all five people onboard, including the 30-year-old pilot, Capt Zainol Afiq Bee Sham.
The other four were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama

Title: PAS at Umno assembly: Friendly visit or ‘preview’ of next election?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — When PAS delegates began arriving at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur last night for Umno’s annual assembly this week, the gesture drew more than polite greetings from party members.
For some Umno delegates, the presence of PAS delegates was a sign that the idea of Malay-Muslim unity was gaining ground again.
For others, it was a matter of returning a courtesy after Umno representatives attended PAS’s
muktamar
last week.
But even those who played down the symbolism acknowledged that the appearance of PAS figures at Umno’s biggest annual gathering carried a different weight this time, coming after Umno and PAS-backed cooperation in Johor and Negri Sembilan and as Melaka emerges as the next electoral test.
Muhamad Ainnul Haziq Mohd Razlan, 28, Kepong Umno division member, said he believed Umno should continue pursuing “
penyatuan ummah
”, or Malay-Muslim political unity, rather than treating it as a temporary political slogan.
“I think we should continue with this unity, and I hope the leaders, the top leadership, will make the best use of this unity. We at the youth level see this unity as something very good,” he told
Malay Mail
on the sidelines of the assembly.
Kepong Umno division member Muhamad Ainnul Haziq Mohd Razlan, 28, speaks during an interview with Malay Mail on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 10, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
For Ainnul, PAS’s decision to send representatives to the Umno assembly was also a positive signal after Umno was invited to attend PAS’s
muktamar
last week.
“When PAS invited us to its
muktamar
last week, that was very good. When someone shows us kindness, we return it,” he said.
He said Umno Youth had also invited PAS Youth representatives to its programmes, describing the exchanges as a positive signal for possible cooperation in the 16th general election.
“Officially, we have to leave that to the top leadership and wait for their answer,” he said.
During the youth assembly on this morning, party youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh welcomed his compatriot from PAS, Afnan Hamimi Taib, describing the latter’s attendance as the culmination of three years of discussions between the two youth wings on national issues.
The distinction, between what members can read into the gestures and what the leadership is prepared to formally commit to, runs through conversations at this year’s assembly.
Hirzan Alam, 29, information chief of the Kota Kemuning Umno Youth division, took a more restrained view, saying PAS’s presence was mainly about returning the favour after Umno representatives attended its
muktamar
.
Kota Kemuning Umno Youth information chief Hirzan Alam, 29, shares his views with Malay Mail during the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 10, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
For Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, a committee member of Umno Youth’s Damansara division, however, the visit could be read as something more.
“To be frank, if you ask me whether PAS coming to any party is more or less a formality to celebrate the relationship, like how we used to invite Harapan to come to WTC to establish unity and whatnot, it is basically more or less a symbolic indicator that we are working together,” he said.
Damansara Umno Youth committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam speaks to Malay Mail on the opening day of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 9, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Najeeh pointed to Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s position that the two parties currently have only a “mutual understanding”, rather than a formal agreement.
“But I think, for a fact, it is a symbol. We might see a shadow of what is going to be the next election’s coalition, like a preview, more or less,” he said.
Another Umno member at the assembly offered a similar reading, saying PAS’s attendance did not itself carry a formal political message as long as no such position had been announced by the top leadership.
PAS Youth delegates are seen seated in the front row at the 2026 Umno Youth General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 10, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
But he said the exchange of delegations nevertheless showed that both parties were serious about the broader agenda of Malay-Muslim unity.
“Umno sent representatives to the
muktamar
, PAS sent representatives to PAU. That shows how serious both parties are about uniting the
ummah
,” he said.
Junaidi Ifdam Jun, 32, from Umno’s Batu Sapi division in Sabah, was more direct in his interpretation.
“For me, it means we will be together. That is what I feel,” he said.
The speculation is taking place against a backdrop that has changed considerably for Umno in recent months.
The party entered this year’s assembly buoyed by victories in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
BN won 48 of Johor’s 56 state seats, including 36 for Umno, while in Negeri Sembilan it secured 18 of 36 seats, with Umno winning all 16 seats it contested. Perikatan Nasional, led by PAS, secured seven.
PAS Muslimat delegates dressed in green sit in the front row among Umno members during the joint opening of the party’s Women, Youth and Puteri wing assemblies at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 9, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
The two coalitions subsequently agreed to work together to form the state administration.
Those results have given Umno delegates a renewed sense of confidence, while also raising the question of how far that momentum can be carried into the next contest.
Melaka is now the obvious test.
The state assembly’s term ends in December, and discussions over possible cooperation for the election are already underway.
Zahid has said negotiations would take place after the assembly is dissolved, while Dr Akmal has been more openly supportive of working with PAS in the state.
Dr Akmal has described Melaka as a test of whether “
penyatuan ummah
” can move beyond rhetoric and become an electoral strategy, pointing to the recent results in Johor and Negeri Sembilan as evidence of what cooperation can achieve.
That makes the PAS delegation’s appearance at the Umno assembly difficult to separate from the electoral calculations ahead, even if no formal pact has been announced.
For delegates like Ainnul, the immediate message is more about keeping the door open.
The exchanges between Umno and PAS have become more visible at a time when both parties are assessing what their next electoral moves could look like.

Title: Court rejects police bid to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand, former TH chairman set for release
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim is expected to be released this evening after his remand period was not extended, said his lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad.
He said the police’s application to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand period for another three days to assist in the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code had been rejected, and the former Baling Member of Parliament is expected to be released before 5pm this evening once the previous remand period expires.
“Our side has strongly objected to the remand extension application on the grounds that our client is always ready and provides full cooperation to the police at any time if needed.
“The investigation can still continue without the need to remand our client. If the authorities require further evidence, he is ready to appear at Bukit Aman at any time,” he said when met by reporters outside the Dang Wangi district police headquarters (IPD) here today.
Abdul Azeez and two former TH officers were previously remanded for two days to assist in the investigation into a fraud case related to TH hibah.
Commenting on the lockup clothes and handcuffs he wore when he was arraigned on charges related to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) case yesterday, Amer Hamzah said Abdul Azeez was at that time under police custody for the remand proceedings.
“Our client only followed the instructions and SOPs set by the police. Therefore, there was no issue of any choice of clothing because he was being remanded by PDRM at the time,” he said.
Amer Hamzah said Abdul Azeez had appeared to give statements more than 10 times before and would continue to fully cooperate with the authorities to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected across KL, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Kuala Muda, Baling, Sik, Yan and Langkawi in Kedah; Timur Laut, Barat Daya, Seberang Perai Utara and Seberang Perai Tengah in Penang; and Kuala Pilah, Seremban, Jempol and Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan.
Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Larut Matang, Selama, Bagan Datuk, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Sepang, Petaling, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Klang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, as well as Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut and Lipis in Pahang.
In Sabah, the affected areas are the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Keningau, Tambunan, Membakut, Beaufort and Sook), West Coast, Tawau (Kunak and Lahad Datu), Sandakan (Kinabatangan) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service operations suspended after fatal helicopter crash, says health minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — All Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in Sarawak have been temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Miri, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today.
In a statement, he said the suspension would allow the relevant authorities to investigate the incident and review existing safety and operational procedures.
“Emergency medical evacuation services for urgent cases will continue through cooperation between the Health Ministry and the Fire and Rescue Department,” he said.
Dzulkefly said the ministry would also discuss the possible use of Armed Forces assets to transport patients requiring emergency treatment to suitable healthcare facilities.
The ministry will conduct a comprehensive assessment of the FDS in Sarawak, covering its contracts, governance, operational safety, coverage needs and the effectiveness of its current service model.
“However, the safety of personnel and patients remains the ministry’s priority, alongside ensuring the continued delivery of healthcare services to rural communities,” he said.
The ministry is also reviewing FDS locations and access methods, including safe and practical transport alternatives, and will provide further updates to the public.

Title: Digital Ministry seeks Budget 2027 incentives to cut cost of digital tools for small traders
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 10 — The Digital Ministry has proposed incentives under Budget 2027 to make digital tools more affordable and encourage their adoption among small traders, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said today.
He said the proposals were presented during a meeting with Finance Ministry officials two weeks ago as part of the government’s Budget engagement process.
“Our proposals largely focus on ensuring that technology capable of helping small traders does not merely exist, but is widely used so that its benefits can be felt,” he told reporters after the launch of a photography and art exhibition, Scars of War, at the Lin Xiang Xiong Art Gallery here.
“The government may need to consider providing incentives to reduce the cost of these tools and related expenses,” he added.
Gobind said the priority was to increase technology adoption and ensure it delivered a tangible impact to businesses and others who needed it.
“I have submitted many proposals, but it is better not to give the details one by one,” he said.
“Let the Finance Ministry make its decision and the prime minister announce it during or before the Budget,” he said.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on October 9.

Title: Hannah Yeoh confirms Pardons Board meeting as speculation over Najib’s bid mounts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has confirmed that the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) will convene tomorrow morning.
Yeoh, who sits on the board as part of her portfolio, declined to disclose details regarding the agenda,
FMT
reported.
“Yes, I can confirm that tomorrow at 8.30am, there will be a pardons board meeting.
“We have been called, and that is all I can comment on for now,” she told reporters after an event today.
FMT
previously reported that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application is expected to be among the primary matters tabled before the board during this week's sitting.
It remains unclear whether the board will arrive at an immediate decision or limit the session to preliminary deliberations.
A separate source indicated that the possibility of allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison term under house arrest may be broached, though it is uncertain whether that option will be formally deliberated during the morning meeting.
Earlier today, Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he was hoping for the “best” outcome tomorrow for Najib’s latest application.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
In 2024, the FT Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
However, Najib and his lawyers subsequently insisted that the partial pardon came with a royal addendum for him to serve out his remaining time at home, eventually suing to have this granted.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.

Title: Puteri Umno wishes Najib well ahead of expected clemency bid discussion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno’s women’s youth wing, Puteri Umno, today extended its best wishes for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid ahead of a meeting expected to discuss his application.
This follows a report by
Free Malaysia Today
that the Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s clemency application during its meeting this week.
Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi expressed the wing’s positive wishes during a press conference at the Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.
“We hope all the best (for Najib).
“And we always prayed for the eased of everything,” Amal said.
Amal met local media after delivering her keynote address at the Puteri Umno General Assembly at WTCKL.
FMT had also previously reported that Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion.
It also reported that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.
He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
The Pardons Board subsequently halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib later withdrew his appeal against the decision.

Title: Zahid to meet Negeri Sembilan MB over statement on proclamation involving Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today he will meet Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim during the party’s general assembly to seek an explanation over his statement regarding a proclamation involving the state’s ruler.
Zahid said Ismail would meet him during the assembly, which began yesterday, although he did not specify when the meeting would take place.
“Yes, he will certainly meet me during this general assembly, and he will give an explanation. I will ask him about the background to his statement,” Zahid told reporters at the media centre here.
Asked when the meeting would take place, Zahid said: “The general assembly has already begun. I can give him a time to meet at any time.”
Ismail had reportedly said he signed a proclamation concerning the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Almarhum Tuanku Munawir, under duress.
He subsequently lodged a police report over the matter.
Zahid had yesterday denied reports that Aminuddin had resigned as menteri besar amid the dispute, saying the state government remained intact.

Article:
