Title: King presents appointment instruments to Court of Appeal, High Court judges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today presented instruments of appointment to two judges at Istana Negara.
The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik.
Present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Court of Appeal President Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah and Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi.
Loke, 64, was appointed Senior Federal Counsel in 2013, a position she held until 2018. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020.
She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.
As a Kuala Lumpur High Court judge, Loke handled Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s judicial review application over an alleged addendum order allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
During her tenure as Senior Federal Counsel, Loke was involved in several high-profile cases, including admiralty proceedings at the Kuala Lumpur High Court to seize the Equanimity, a vessel allegedly built using funds from 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB).
She also handled the Sulu claim and lawsuits filed against the Malaysian government over the disappearance of Malaysia Airlines flight MH370.
Meanwhile, Yap, 53, holds a Bachelor of Laws from the University of Sydney and a Diploma in International Arbitration from the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators.
She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on Aug 28, 2024, before taking up the same position at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Nov 3, 2025. — Bernama

Title: Perak Assembly approves PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul as senator with 33 votes
Article:
IPOH, September 10 — The Perak Legislative Assembly today approved the appointment of Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator after he secured 33 votes in a secret ballot.
The 38-year-old defeated Perak PAS Dewan Ulama chairman Muhammad Zulkifli Muhammad Zakaria, the Opposition coalition’s candidate, who received 26 votes.
The election was held following the expiry of former senator and Perak Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusuf Rawa’s term on May 24.
A total of 59 votes were cast by members of the Legislative Assembly.
The motion for the appointment was tabled by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and supported by Teja assemblyman Sandrea Ng Shy Ching (PKR).
Mohamad Hairul’s nomination was proposed by Ng and seconded by Lintang assemblyman Datuk Mohd Zolkfaly Haron (BN).
A Perak native, Mohamad Hairul holds a degree in Political Science from Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).
He currently serves as chief special officer at the Office of Tambun MP, a position held by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
His previous appointments include serving on the Perak Water Board and as a non-executive and independent committee member of Panel International Bhd.
Mohamad Hairul has also served as Perak PKR chairman since 2024.

Title: Transboundary haze discussed on sidelines of Asean health ministers meeting, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The transboundary haze issue is not on the formal agenda of the 17th ASEAN Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, but it is being discussed on the sidelines among health ministers of member states.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the matter could subsequently be taken up at the senior officers’ meeting.
“…we (will) do a side discussion among our ministers. That one we will continue to discuss. But perhaps, in our subsequent meeting, the senior officers’ meeting can carry this through. But as an agenda, unfortunately we are not there,” he said in a press conference after the launch of ASHA 2026-2030 here today.
However, Dzulkefly said the issue could be addressed within the scope of the existing health clusters.
When asked whether Malaysia planned to hold bilateral discussions with Indonesia on the haze issue, the health minister said: “We raised it, but we must follow through again.”
Yesterday, Communications Minister and Madani Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia is still awaiting confirmation from the Indonesian authorities before deploying assets that can be used to help tackle forest fires in the country, which had caused transboundary haze. — Bernama

Title: Dr Akmal: Umno Youth ready to work with PAS in Melaka, state is next test for Malay-Muslim unity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno Youth is ready to work with PAS in the coming Melaka state election and believes its support among young voters can help deliver another electoral victory, Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said today.
Dr Akmal, who is also the Merlimau assemblyman, described Melaka as a crucial test of whether “penyatuan ummah” — the idea of uniting Malay-Muslim political parties — could be translated from political rhetoric into an actual electoral strategy.
“Melaka isn’t just a state, it’s a test — to see if we can change the reality, and penyatuan becomes a basis and not just an idea.
“Johor has decided and Negri Sembilan has decided. So I ask Datuk Seri (Zahid), Melaka should be blue as well,” he said during his speech at the Umno Youth general assembly.He said Umno Youth was prepared to repeat the strong performance it recorded among young voters in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections.
Dr Akmal said the wing was prepared to cooperate with PAS in Melaka, while making clear that he was not seeking candidacy for himself.
“If we work with PAS in Melaka, Datuk Seri, I repeat, at this stage as the leader of Umno Youth I do not want to become a candidate if PH is a candidate there.
“However I believe you are smart, and I’m sure you don’t want to see the Umno Youth chief not compete. We will be there with you,” he said, referring to Umno president and BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
Dr Akmals’ remarks come amid continuing discussions within Umno and BN over possible cooperation for the Melaka election.
Zahid said earlier this month that he had given Melaka Chief Minister and state BN chief Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh the mandate to negotiate cooperation with any party, with the eventual partner expected to be one that could help BN retain control of the state.
Zahid has also said formal negotiations would take place after the Melaka state assembly is dissolved, meaning no final electoral pact had been announced at the time of Dr Akmal’s speech.
Dr Akmal’s position was more specific, however, with the Umno Youth chief openly arguing for cooperation with PAS and presenting Melaka as the next opportunity to test the strategy after Johor and Negri Sembilan.
He said the wing also wanted the party to address issues affecting young Malaysians, including housing, childcare and the financial pressures faced by young families.
Dr Akmal’s Melaka pitch therefore combined a call for cooperation with PAS with a broader demand that Umno’s youth wing be given a meaningful role in shaping the party’s election platform.
The Melaka state assembly’s current term ends in December, while BN won 21 of the 28 seats in the 2021 state election, compared with five won by Pakatan Harapan and two by Perikatan Nasional.
During today’s assembly, Dr Akmal gave a particularly warm welcome to PAS Youth chief Afnan Hamimi Taib, describing the latter’s attendance as the culmination of three years of discussions between the two youth wings on national issues.
He said their pursuit of Malay-Muslim political unity predated the recent Johor and Negri Sembilan elections, where cooperation between Umno and PAS had already produced results.

Title: Malaysia’s unsold completed homes rise 8.6pc in H1 2026, but market is resilient, says finance minister II
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — More completed homes and serviced apartments were left unsold in the first half of 2026 compared with the preceding six months, according to the Property Market Report for the First Half of 2026.
The report, released by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) today, showed that the number of unsold completed homes rose by 8.6 per cent, from 30,471 units in the second half of 2025 to 33,094 units in the first half of 2026.
Their combined value increased slightly from RM17.73 billion to RM17.78 billion.
Despite the rise in unsold properties, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the overall property market remained resilient, recording 187,320 transactions worth RM105.12 billion between January and June 2026.
Residential properties accounted for 59.3 per cent of all transactions, with 110,998 deals recorded, and contributed 44.8 per cent of the total transaction value, or RM47.11 billion.
“Although there were some marginal adjustments, the property market remain steady due to stable price movements and transaction activities as well as active construction activities.
“The stability is also influenced by the country’s monetary policy that maintained the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent, injecting confidence to both financiers and buyers,” he said before launching the report at the National Valuation Institute (Inspen) in Kajang, Selangor, today.
High-rise properties made up the largest portion of the unsold homes at 43.4 per cent, followed by terraced houses at 34.9 per cent.
About 37.3 per cent were priced at RM300,000 and below, while 38 per cent had been launched between six and 10 years ago.
Serviced apartments, which are classified separately under commercial properties, recorded a sharper increase of 24.7 per cent, from 18,752 unsold units worth RM15.42 billion in the second half of 2025 to 23,375 units worth RM19.33 billion in the first half of 2026.
More than half of the unsold serviced apartments, or 55.2 per cent, were priced between RM500,001 and RM1 million, while 71.1 per cent had been launched between six and 10 years ago.
Johor had the most unsold completed homes and serviced apartments, with 4,222 and 9,946 units, respectively.
At the same time, Johor recorded 6,697 new residential launches, the second-highest number after Selangor’s 8,354 units, while Penang ranked third with 2,878 units.
Homes priced between RM500,001 and RM1 million formed the largest segment of new launches nationwide, accounting for 10,853 units, or 39 per cent of the total.

Title: Kangar Bersatu deputy chief, 90 branch chiefs leave party over loss of trust in leadership
Article:
KANGAR, Sept 10 — Kangar Bersatu division deputy chief Faisol Rahman, together with the division committee and 90 of its 99 branch chiefs, announced tonight that they are leaving the party with immediate effect.
Also announcing their departure were the division’s Armada, Srikandi and Srikandi Muda leadership lines, including Armada Kangar deputy chief Mohd Firdaus Ismail and all Armada committee members.
Speaking at a press conference in Kuala Perlis last night, Faisol, on behalf of the group, said the move, however, did not involve any Bersatu Members of Parliament or state assemblymen within the division’s committee.
“This decision was made after careful deliberation, taking into account current developments and the views of the grassroots, who have lost faith in the central leadership.
“Having spent so long building the party at the grassroots level, we feel that trust in the party’s leadership has been lost,” he said.
Faisol said certain matters concerning the party’s direction, organisational management and leadership approach were no longer aligned with their hopes and aspirations as leaders at the division and branch levels.
He said the strength of a political party begins with trust between its leadership and grassroots members, and when that trust erodes, it is time for them to take a clear stand.
In light of this, he said they would be joining Parti Wawasan Negara, which is led by Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
Meanwhile, Perlis Bersatu leadership body chief Izizam Ibrahim said he viewed the resignations and departures positively, as it would enable an effective cleansing to strengthen the party in the state.
Izizam said that under Bersatu’s constitution, any resignation or vacancy within a division does not dissolve the division. Instead, a new organising committee will be formed to restructure the division’s leadership. — Bernama

Title: MOH still awaiting official post-mortem report on five Long Lellang crash victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is still awaiting the official report on the post-mortem findings of the five victims who were killed in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was still awaiting official confirmation on the matter before providing further details to the public.
“As soon as we get everything officially, Datuk DG (Health director-general) will provide an explanation.
“Although we have heard about it, we have yet to receive anything official,” he told reporters at a press conference after the opening ceremony of the 17th Asean Health Ministers’ Meeting (AHMM) here today.
Also present were MOH secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad and Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abdul Wahab.
Meanwhile, Dr Mahathar said the Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah had explained the procedures and processes related to the post-mortems in a statement yesterday, but the ministry was still awaiting a further announcement on the matter.
Yesterday, Mohamad Zainal confirmed that the five bodies of the victims killed in the helicopter crash had been successfully recovered from the crash site and flown from Long Lellang to Miri for post-mortems and related procedures. — Bernama
